Source: China Ministry of Foreign Affairs Treaty Database (条约数据库)
Coverage: Bilateral and multilateral treaties and some cooperation documents. 31 records match 文物, 文化遗产, 考古, 世界遗产 or 非物质文化遗产: 6 on illicit trafficking, 8 heritage-cooperation memoranda, 11 exhibition agreements from 1973-76.
How systematic: Highly structured: title, type, field, date signed, date in force, record ID, full text.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Keyword search by web form (tested 2026-10-05); results can be collected page by page.
Framing notes: Incomplete after 2009: it holds 5 country agreements on illicit trafficking plus the US memorandum, while officials cite 26-27. Titles shift from 'exhibition of unearthed relics' (1970s) to 'preventing theft and illicit export' and 'cooperating to protect heritage' (2005-09).

Source: Official counts of bilateral agreements on illicit trafficking of cultural property
Coverage: 26 countries as of November 2023 (Beijing News); 27 as of September 2026 (Yangcheng Evening News).
How systematic: Counts only. No public list of the countries found.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Manual; ask NCHA or assemble from news.

Source: US State Department: cultural property agreements and import restrictions
Coverage: 41 countries with US agreements or restrictions. China: memorandum of 14 January 2009, extended 2014, 2019 and 2024.
How systematic: Structured list by country with Federal Register notices and designated lists.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Web page (archived copy covering 2012 to May 2025) and Federal Register.
Framing notes: Counterparty view of the same agreement; Chinese press reports more than 700 items returned in over 20 batches since 2009.

Source: UNESCO Database of National Cultural Heritage Laws (China page)
Coverage: 19 Chinese legal documents, from 1928 regulations to the Law on Protection of Cultural Relics (1982, 2002, 2007); includes bilateral agreements with Egypt (2010) and Switzerland (2013).
How systematic: Structured table: document, year, theme, category, language, with PDFs.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Web page with PDF links; same structure for every country.
Framing notes: Neutral. Lets you compare host-country heritage laws in the same format.

Source: World Heritage Committee sessions archive and decisions database
Coverage: Every Committee, Bureau and General Assembly session since 1977 with documents, decisions and records. Sessions held in China: 28th (Suzhou, 2004) and 44th (Fuzhou, 2021).
How systematic: Highly structured by session code; decisions have stable IDs.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Web pages; UNESCO's terms on scraping apply (see Data Access sheet).
Framing notes: Official wording of decisions; useful for when terms such as 'Silk Roads' enter decisions.

Coverage: Project-level data by donor and sector. Example: China Funds-in-Trust (Quanzhou) for Capacity-Building on World Heritage in Africa, USD 1,000,000, 11 March 2025 to 10 March 2028.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Download or page per project ID.
Framing notes: Shows a Chinese city (Quanzhou, a 2021 World Heritage site) as named donor for African nominations.

Source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre partner page: Government of China
Coverage: China-funded World Heritage work in Africa since 2014: nomination support in Chad, Cameroon, Nigeria, Benin and Togo; capacity building in Uganda, Congo, Ethiopia, Gabon, Mali, Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal and Tanzania; 2019 UNESCO-Africa-China Forum.
How systematic: One page per partner with linked news and events. No amounts given.
Framing notes: China as funder of other countries' nominations, not of 'Chinese' sites.

Source: UNESCO category 2 centres hosted by China
Coverage: World Heritage centres: WHITR-AP (training and research, Shanghai) and HIST (space technologies). Intangible heritage: CRIHAP (training centre for Asia-Pacific, set up 2012; a 2019 workshop drew beneficiaries from Cambodia, Kazakhstan, Mongolia, Myanmar, Nepal and others).
How systematic: Each centre publishes activity news and annual reports; no shared database.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Manual, or scrape each centre's news.
Framing notes: China as a regional training provider.

Source: Alliance for Cultural Heritage in Asia (ACHA) and the Asian Fund for Cultural Heritage Conservation
Owner type: China-led intergovernmental organisation; fund run under the China Foundation for Cultural Heritage Conservation
Coverage: ACHA became an intergovernmental organisation on 19 June 2024 (20 members, observers and partners at that date). Fund rounds: first 15 projects, RMB 4.6364 million, 8 countries (announced 2024); 15 more for 2024-2025 (announced November 2025, Chongqing).
How systematic: Project lists announced through state media; no public project database found.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Manual from news; ask ACHA for lists.
Framing notes: 'Asian' framing: projects in Armenia, Azerbaijan, Cambodia, UAE, Sri Lanka, Syria, Uzbekistan. New committee on 'Austronesian peoples and maritime civilisation'.

Source: Belt and Road Forum deliverables lists (2017, 2019, 2023)
Coverage: Numbered lists of agreed projects. The October 2023 list includes the Maritime Silk Road transnational nomination, a China-Saudi joint excavation at Serrin port, and an archaeological park at Nateshwar, Bangladesh.
How systematic: Semi-structured numbered lists, one document per forum.
Framing notes: Heritage listed as a Belt and Road deliverable alongside infrastructure.
Reliability: High for intent; not for delivery.

Coverage: Guangming Daily (2 January 2025): restoration aid in Cambodia, Mongolia, Uzbekistan (Khiva), Nepal, Myanmar (Bagan) and Kyrgyzstan.
Framing notes: 'One flower alone is not spring; a hundred flowers in bloom fill the garden' (civilisational diversity).

Source: Chinese companies and private donors in heritage work abroad
Coverage: No source found that lists Chinese companies restoring or funding heritage sites abroad.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Places to look next: implementing-agency field in AidData (1c sheet); Ministry of Commerce aid tenders; donor lists of the China Foundation for Cultural Heritage Conservation.

Source: Regional summit outcome lists (China-Central Asia Summit, FOCAC action plans)
Coverage: Outcome lists and action plans that may contain heritage clauses.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Not yet read; test in a later pass.
